controls.title: Basic Controls
controls.description: Learn your goals as mayor and how to plan before advancing time. After exploring what the city’s information means, what each button does and how to move the camera, you will extend a road to create a new residential area and provide it with homes, electricity and water.

step1.title: Build a city as mayor
step1.role: In City Genesis, you grow a city as its mayor. You plan roads and facilities, decide how land is used, set taxes and allocate money to public services. Your job is to create the conditions that support residents and businesses. Press “Next” to continue.
step1.goal: Aim for a city where residents can live comfortably and safely. Provide homes and jobs, electricity, water and healthcare. Growing the city also takes money. Consider both people’s lives and the city’s finances when deciding what to improve.
step1.epoch: Time advances one month at a time. First set budgets and construction plans, then press “Start” when you are ready. Construction and the activities of residents and businesses advance; review the results before making your next plans. The date stays still until you start, so take your time.
step1.epoch_week: Time advances one week at a time. First set budgets and construction plans, then press “Start” when you are ready. Construction and the activities of residents and businesses advance; review the results before making your next plans. The date stays still until you start, so take your time.

step2.title: Read the city from the cockpit
step2.tools: The cockpit at the bottom of the screen helps you check the city and decide what to do next. “View” uses colors to help find shortages and problem areas. “Map” shows where places are across the city, helping you find your way as it grows.
step2.tracking: “Citizen list” lets you find residents by name and keeps residents you want to revisit. Add someone to tracking from their citizen details, then use this button to return to their information and commutes. Explore individual lives behind the citywide figures.
step2.bulldozer: “Bulldozer” removes empty parcels and cancels planned buildings and roads. Press the button, then click a target in the 3D view; press it again to leave the mode. To remove a completed building or road, open its details and choose demolition.
step2.services: The lightning and water-drop gauges show how much room your electricity and water supplies have to grow. As they fill, demand is approaching capacity. Click them to review public facilities, and check whether you need more supply before expanding the city.
step2.score: “Score” summarizes how satisfied residents are with life in your city. Higher is better. Homes, jobs, healthcare and a pleasant living environment help improve it. If it falls, look for the difficulties residents are facing.
step2.budget: “Budget” shows next month’s expected expenses relative to last month’s income. When the gauge swings to the right, expenses exceed income. Conversely, when it swings to the left, you have money to spare. Check it before advancing time.
step2.budget_week: “Budget” shows next week’s expected expenses relative to last week’s income. When the gauge swings to the right, expenses exceed income. Conversely, when it swings to the left, you have money to spare. Check it before advancing time.
step2.budgetChanges: More construction, higher facility operation and faster construction increase the money needed and raise the budget gauge. Lower operation or slower construction can reduce expected costs. When tax revenue increases, the gauge goes down even if expenses stay the same.
step2.budgetPlanning: A low gauge means you have money available for the city. Consider investing in missing services or facilities you will need soon.
step2.date: The date shows how far the city’s time has advanced. Use it to track construction progress and seasonal changes. It stays still while you plan and updates when you advance time with “Start”.
step2.climate: The temperature, rainfall, sunlight and wind panel shows this month’s average climate. These conditions affect farming, wind power and solar power. If crops or electricity production are low, check the climate too.
step2.climate_week: The temperature, rainfall, sunlight and wind panel shows this week’s average climate. These conditions affect farming, wind power and solar power. If crops or electricity production are low, check the climate too.
step2.climateEffects: Weak sunlight reduces solar output, and weak wind reduces wind output. Temperature and rainfall also affect farming. Click the climate panel to see how this month’s conditions affect each facility’s production efficiency. Plan facilities with seasonal changes in supply in mind.
step2.climateEffects_week: Weak sunlight reduces solar output, and weak wind reduces wind output. Temperature and rainfall also affect farming. Click the climate panel to see how this week’s conditions affect each facility’s production efficiency. Plan facilities with seasonal changes in supply in mind.
step2.notifications: The number on “Notifications” counts warnings and cautions to review. A red number and flashing button mean city functions are being disrupted and need prompt attention. Yellow numbers indicate cautions, such as preparing for growth or problems that take time to improve. Press the button to read them.
step2.notificationActions: When a notice identifies a facility or district, click its row to inspect it. Respond to the cause: connect missing power lines or arrange supplies for a facility short of materials. Notices about ongoing problems disappear when their cause is resolved. After taking action, check next month’s results.

step3.title: Change the view to find problems
step3.open: Power shortages and traffic congestion can be hard to spot from the city’s appearance. Use “View” to show the information you need on the map. Press “View” in the cockpit to open the panel.
step3.tabs: The vertical tabs let you choose what to inspect, such as buildings, roads, parcels or districts. You can also hide unwanted objects when overlapping information makes the view hard to read. Press “Next” to explore the display options.
step3.modes: The buttons in each tab choose which information colors the objects. Find busy roads or troubled buildings and use them as clues for your next action. Click an object in the 3D view to inspect it further. Leave the panel open and press “Next”.

step4.title: Discover your city-building tools
step4.grading: Let’s explore the buttons on the left from top to bottom. “Earthworks” levels slopes for building or reclaims land from the sea. It creates room for growth when you need more homes or workplaces but have too little usable land.
step4.road: “Roads, Rail & Infrastructure” creates routes for people, goods, power and water. Connect homes and workplaces with roads, link distant places with rail, and connect facilities with power lines and pipes. These networks support travel, trade and utility supplies.
step4.land: “Land Parcels” prepares sites for buildings. Empty land alone is not a building site. More homes and large facilities both need sites with enough room for them.
step4.landDevelopment: Parcels provide space for city construction and for private homes and businesses to develop. Private buildings grow according to demand and district building rules. When you want more homes or jobs, check that enough vacant parcels are available.
step4.district: “District” lets you manage parts of the city with different priorities, such as a residential neighborhood or an industrial area. Each district can restrict the types of buildings allowed, giving the whole neighborhood a suitable direction for development.
step4.districtRules: District details let you choose which types of buildings are allowed. Use them according to the kind of city you want to grow, such as keeping factories out of a residential neighborhood. You can also compare population and living conditions between districts to decide where support is needed.
step4.construction: “Construction” plans buildings the city needs. You can build homes, workplaces, hospitals, schools and power plants. Use it to provide more housing and jobs or fill gaps in healthcare, education, electricity and other services.
step4.transport: “Public Transport” helps residents travel by bus or rail. You can set routes and stops, and adjust fares and service intervals. Linking homes with workplaces and schools helps reduce the burden of commuting.
step4.propPlacement: “Prop Placement” adds trees, rocks and other scenery. Use it to add greenery to streets or decorate the terrain.
step4.constructionProjects: “Construction Projects” gathers planned and ongoing works in one place. Review progress and costs to decide which works to advance.
step4.regulation: “Regulations” sets rules for living and working in the city, including speed limits, working hours, immigration and social security. Adjust them to suit your priorities for safety, time to enjoy life and city growth.
step4.stat: “Statistics” helps you evaluate your decisions. Charts show changes in population, income, commuting, resident satisfaction, and the size of the economy and prices. After changing policies or facilities, check whether life is improving and what is still missing. That completes the buttons on the left.

step5.title: Run your plans and review results
step5.flow: After checking the city and planning construction and budgets, use “Start” in the cockpit to advance time. Work progresses, residents work, businesses produce, and finances and scores change. Some plans need several months to show their effects.
step5.execute: After advancing time, review the results and notices. Address problems in your next plans, then advance time again. Grow the city by repeating “plan, advance, review”. You do not need to press “Start” here. Press “Next” to learn the camera controls.

step6.title: Move the camera
step6.description: You can move the camera like this: drag with the left button to move the view, drag with the right button to rotate, W/A/S/D (or the arrow keys) to move, Q/E to rotate, R/F to change the height, and the mouse wheel to zoom. Try it freely, then press "Next".

step7.title: Fly mode and cinema mode
step7.description: The camera has two special modes. "Fly mode" starts with Shift+F: move along your view with W/A/S/D, look around with the mouse, and go up or down with R/F. Press Esc to leave it. "Cinema mode" starts from the button in the top-right corner of the screen and lets you circle around the city. Look around with the mouse; Shift switches between orbiting and travelling, Space pauses, Backspace reverses, and Esc exits. The on-screen panels are hidden while either mode is on and come back when you press Esc. When you've tried them, exit both modes and press "Next".

step8.title: See the city boundary
step8.description: We moved the camera to the east edge of the city. The area you can use as a city is this rectangle where detailed terrain exists, and the camera cannot leave it either. That's all for the screen and controls. Next, let's actually create a new residential area. Press “Next”.

step9.title: Extend the Road
step9.description: Now let's build a residential area to welcome new residents. Homes and workplaces are no use unless roads connect them: people can't come and go, and goods can't arrive. First, extend the town’s east–west street to the west to open a way into the new neighborhood. Press “Roads, Rail & Infrastructure” on the icon panel to open the construction panel.

step10.title: Complete the Road
step10.description: The road is still “Construction Planned”. A planned road can't be used yet — people and cars can only use it once the work is finished. Press “Start” in the cockpit 2–3 times to advance time and wait for it to be completed. Construction costs money every month while it is underway.
step10.description_week: The road is still “Construction Planned”. A planned road can't be used yet — people and cars can only use it once the work is finished. Press “Start” in the cockpit 2–3 times to advance time and wait for it to be completed. Construction costs money every week while it is underway.

step11.title: Create Parcels
step11.description: The road is ready. Next, prepare parcels to serve as building sites. Buildings can only stand on parcels, and a parcel facing a road lets people and goods come and go. Press “Land Parcels” on the icon panel.
step11.create: Make sure “Create Along Road” is selected, then click the road you extended in the 3D view. When red outlines line up along the road, confirm to create the parcels.

step12.title: Create a District
step12.description: Before building, decide what this street should become. Without a plan, a factory might go up right next to the homes. Such plans are made per “District”. Districts are assigned road by road, and a parcel belongs to the district of the road it faces. Press “District” on the icon panel to open the Edit Districts window: right now the whole town is a single district.
step12.create: Use the “Street Side” brush. Switch the tool to “Create New District”, hold Ctrl and drag along the road you extended. Both sides of the road you paint, along with the parcels facing them, become a new district.

step13.title: District Created
step13.description: You've separated the new street from the town center as its own district. You can check population and prices per district and decide which buildings may be built there, so each area can grow in the way that suits it. Once you've checked it, close the Edit Districts window.

step14.title: Open District Details
step14.description: Let's make the new district a residential area. Show the districts with the icon at the bottom left of the screen, then click the label of the district you just created to open its details.

step15.title: Make It Residential
step15.description: The building regulations near the bottom of the panel choose which buildings may be built on this district's parcels. We want a calm place to live here, so click every building other than “Apartment” and “House” to disable them.

step16.title: Check a Parcel
step16.description: A district's regulations apply to every parcel in it. Click the parcel with the yellow marker to open its details.

step17.title: Regulation Applied
step17.description: Near the bottom of the parcel panel, you can see the district's regulation allowing only “Apartment” and “House”. Now only homes can be built on this street. Instead of setting parcels one by one, deciding a district's direction makes the whole street follow it.

step18.title: Build Homes
step18.description: Now let's provide homes. Housing is normally built automatically by the private sector when people want to live here, but public housing built by the city quickly makes up for a shortage. Let's build a public apartment building here. Press “Construction” on the icon panel.
step18.select: Choose “Apartment Complex” in the “Residential” category, click any parcel in the new district as the site, and confirm.

step19.title: Complete the Homes
step19.description: Like roads, buildings can't be lived in just because they're planned. An apartment building takes more than half a year to finish. Press “Start” to advance time and wait for it to be completed.

step20.title: Check for Electricity
step20.description: Homes alone don't make a life: people also need electricity and water. This town has no power plant and no water supply yet. Click the apartment building with the yellow marker, where the townspeople live, to open its details, pick one of the tenants in the “Building Info” tab, then open its “Supply, Demand & Trade” tab: you can confirm that the Acquired amount of Electricity is 0.

step21.title: Build a Solar Power Plant
step21.description: To deliver electricity, you first need a power plant to generate it. Build a “Solar Power Plant” on the parcel with the yellow marker. It would normally take time to complete, but since this is a tutorial, the construction period is skipped.

step22.title: Build a Substation
step22.description: The high-voltage electricity from a power plant can't be used by households as it is. A substation converts it into power homes can use and distributes it to the surrounding buildings connected by road. Build an “Electrical Substation” on the parcel with the yellow marker near the apartment building.

step23.title: Connect with a Power Line
step23.description: Even when the power plant and the substation are apart, a route for the electricity connects them. Open “Roads, Rail & Infrastructure” on the icon panel, choose “Power Transmission Line” under “Electricity”, and draw a line from the solar power plant's connection terminal to the substation's terminal. A straight line between the terminals does it in one go.

step24.title: Confirm the Power Supply
step24.description: Once connected, make sure electricity is really flowing. Press “Start” to advance time, click the substation to open its details, and in the “Supply, Demand & Trade” tab check that the Received amount of High-Voltage Electricity isn't 0. It may take a few months for the plant to start up and the power to arrive.

step25.title: Power Reaches Homes
step25.description: From the apartment building's details, open a tenant's “Supply, Demand & Trade” tab as you did at first, and check that the Acquired amount of Electricity is no longer 0. It may take another month or two to reach households. Generate it at a power plant, carry it over power lines, distribute it from a substation — only when all three are connected does electricity reach homes.

step26.title: Find a Water Source
step26.description: Next is water. Tap water is groundwater pumped up and sent to the town. First, find out where water can be pumped. Press “View” in the cockpit to open the View panel.
step26.show: Choose “Natural Resources” from the vertical tabs and switch it to “Visible”. Water sources appear in light blue on the map. Click the water source with the yellow marker to open its details.

step27.title: Build a Groundwater Pump
step27.description: A groundwater pump draws water up from underground, so it must be built where there is a water source. It also needs electricity and workers to run, which is why we brought in power first. Build a “Groundwater Well Pump” on the parcel with the yellow marker on top of the water source. Since this is a tutorial, the construction period is skipped.

step28.title: Build a Water Pumping Station
step28.description: Pumped water can't be handed to households as it is. Just as a substation distributes electricity, a water pumping station delivers water to the surrounding buildings connected by road. Build a “Water Pumping Station” on the parcel with the yellow marker near the apartment building.

step29.title: Connect with a Pipe
step29.description: You need a pipe to carry the water from the groundwater pump to the pumping station. Open “Roads, Rail & Infrastructure” on the icon panel, choose “Water Aqueduct Pipe” under “Water”, and lay it from the groundwater pump's connection terminal to the pumping station's terminal.

step30.title: Confirm the Water Supply
step30.description: Press “Start” to advance time, click the water pumping station to open its details, and in the “Supply, Demand & Trade” tab check that the Received amount of High-Pressure Water isn't 0. It may take a few months for workers to gather at the groundwater pump and for the water to arrive.

step31.title: The Basics Are in Place
step31.description: Water has reached the pumping station, so homes around it can now use tap water. Lay roads, prepare parcels, decide each district's direction, build homes, and bring in electricity and water — that is the basic flow of city building. Press “Next” to finish the Basic Controls tutorial.

scenario4.title: Build a Railway
scenario4.description: We want to connect the residential area and workplaces by railway, but private buildings and a public hospital obstruct the route. In this tutorial you will learn land acquisition, public-facility demolition, elevated track above roads, platforms and stations, a depot, curve and grade adjustment, power connection and opening a service.

step1.description: Open Roads, Rail & Infrastructure → Railways. Build the high-standard elevated side platforms on the west side of town and the double-track side platforms on the east side. Left-click both marked endpoints at 6m, right-click to finish the shape, then confirm.

step6.title: Lay track directly above the main road

step8.title: Shape the curved climbing branch
step8.description: Choose Railway Track. Start at the depot’s eastern ground-level terminal, make a broad loop east through the northeast marker, and connect to the main line’s merge point at 6m. complete.title: Tutorial Complete

guide.openRoad: Open the construction panel using the road icon.
guide.selectRoad: Select the ground-level two-lane street. Only the required variant is available.
guide.placeStart: Left-click inside the cyan circle to place the start of the road.
guide.placeEnd: Left-click inside the yellow circle to place the end of the road.
guide.finalizeRoad: Right-click in the 3D view to finish the road shape.
guide.confirmRoad: Confirm in the construction panel to save the road, then press "Next".

trade.title: Start international trade
trade.description: A local factory wants to reach overseas customers. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to export food through a port and import goods by freight rail from a neighboring country.

step1.description: An export terminal is needed to ship the food produced on this island overseas. Build a "Container Terminal" on the coastal parcel with the yellow marker. Since this is a tutorial, the construction period is skipped.
step1.title: Build a container port

step2.description: It takes a few months for the factory's production and transport to get going, so advance time and look at the port's export results. Close the Container Terminal's details once and reopen them, and you can see its import and export results in the Cargo tab.
step2.title: Confirm food exports

step3.description: You now have a place to import and export by ship. Next, let's build a place to import and export goods by rail. Build an "International Freight Station" on the parcel with the yellow marker along the road. At the eastern border, there is a railway leading into the neighboring country and a border freight station.
step3.title: Build an international freight station

step4.open: Open "Roads, Rail & Infrastructure" on the icon panel and choose "Container Freight Platform" under "Railways".
step4.place: Lay a platform north of the international freight station, parallel to it. Left-click inside the cyan circle (west) to place the start and inside the yellow circle (east) to place the end, then right-click in the 3D view to finish the shape. Switch "Platform Side" to "Inside" and check that the platform is on the station building's side (the south side) before confirming. When you're done, press "Next".
step4.title: Build a platform beside the station

step5.description: Press "Back" to return to the list, choose "Railway Track", and lay track from the east end of the platform to the west end of the track coming in from the border freight station outside the city.
step5.title: Lay track to the border

step6.title: Build a Depot
step6.description: Build a "Rail Depot" on the parcel with the yellow marker along the track. Press "Next" and, since this is a tutorial, the construction period is skipped and the depot is completed.

step7.title: Connect the Depot to the Main Line
step7.description: Lay a siding from the connection terminal at the east end of the depot to the main line. Join the main line at a shallow angle heading east rather than at a right angle. When you're done, press "Next".

step8.description: Open "Roads, Rail & Infrastructure" on the icon panel and use "Power Line" under "Electricity" to connect the connection terminal of the solar power plant east of town to the depot's connection terminal.
step8.title: Supply power to the depot

step9.description: In "Public Transport", press "+ New line" and choose "International Freight Line" as the line type. Place stops on the platforms of the international freight station and the border freight station, and open the line. Trains cannot pass each other on single track, so set the target headway to 45 minutes so that one train can make the round trip.
step9.title: Open the international freight line

step10.description: Advance time and confirm that freight trains start running on the international freight line. It takes a few months for the depot to hire staff, buy materials and prepare the vehicles.
step10.title: Run the freight trains

highway.title: Build a motorway
highway.description: The town needs another route for vehicles as it grows. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to build an elevated highway over a local road and connect them with ramps to create an interchange.

step1.title: Cross above the street
step1.open: Cross the central street with an elevated motorway. Open "Roads, Rail & Infrastructure" on the icon panel and choose the two-lane motorway under "Motorways".
step1.start: Left-click inside the cyan circle to place the start of the motorway. It snaps to a viaduct 7 m above the ground.
step1.end: Left-click inside the yellow circle to place the end. It snaps to the same 7 m height on the far side of the street.
step1.confirm: Confirm in the construction panel to save the motorway, then press "Next". Since this is a tutorial, construction time is skipped and it is completed right away.

step2.title: Name the motorway
step2.description: You can manage roads by giving them names. At the very top of the details window of the motorway you built, the road it belongs to is currently "None (not part of a road)", so give it any name you like.

step3.title: Build a ramp
step3.description: Build a ramp to connect to the street. Select "Ramp" as the road type, and connect a smoothly curved ramp from the position of the yellow marker on the screen to the motorway.

step4.title: Inspect the interchange
step4.description: You can open the interchange detail panel by clicking "IC1" displayed around the ramp. Confirm that the street and motorway are connected.

mining.title: Mine resources
mining.description: Valuable resources lie beneath the island, but there's no way to haul them out. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to set up a mine, freight railway, and port to extract ore, transport it, and export it overseas.

step1.description: Enable natural resources and open the detail panel of the southeastern ore deposit.
step1.title: Inspect the ore vein

step2.description: Build a Mine on the yellow plot over the southeastern ore vein. Since this is a tutorial, construction time is skipped.
step2.title: Build a mine

step3.description: Build an Ore loading station on the large existing plot southeast of the mine. An ore loading station lets you load the ore extracted at the mine onto trains.
step3.title: Build a loading station next to the mine

step4.description: Build an Ore unloading station on the large existing plot south of the harbor. An ore unloading station lets you carry out the ore brought in by train.
step4.title: Build an unloading station near the port

step5.description: Build a Bulk port on the yellow coastal plot.
step5.title: Build a bulk port

step6.open: Choose Ore freight platform and connect each pair of markers southwest of the loading station and south of the unloading station. Face the platforms toward their facilities.
step6.loading: Choose Ore freight platform and connect each pair of markers southwest of the loading station and south of the unloading station. Face the platforms toward their facilities.
step6.unloading: Choose Ore freight platform and connect each pair of markers southwest of the loading station and south of the unloading station. Face the platforms toward their facilities.
step6.title: Build platforms beside the stations

step7.town: Lay freight track from the eastern harbor-platform end, passing south of the road’s midpoint, to the northwestern mountain-platform end. The track is not connected yet, so lay it yourself. Use curves to align the direction of travel, set Terrain Follow to "No Follow" for the climb, and adjust grade and radius until the red violations disappear. Add intermediate points so each span is 500m or less.
step7.climb: Lay freight track from the eastern harbor-platform end, passing south of the road’s midpoint, to the northwestern mountain-platform end. The track is not connected yet, so lay it yourself. Use curves to align the direction of travel, set Terrain Follow to "No Follow" for the climb, and adjust grade and radius until the red violations disappear. Add intermediate points so each span is 500m or less.
step7.title: Connect the two stations by rail

step8.title: Build a Depot
step8.description: Build a Rail depot on the existing plot southwest of the harbor. Orient it so that a track can be led from the connection terminal at its eastern end to the harbor-side platform.

step9.title: Connect the Depot to the Main Line
step9.description: Connect the depot’s eastern terminal to the western harbor-platform end with a smooth shallow-angle branch.

step10.description: Connect the existing solar plant terminal to the depot’s eastern shared terminal with a power line.
step10.title: Supply power to the depot

step11.description: Create an Ore transport line, place stops on both ore freight platforms, and click the first stop to close the return loop. Trains cannot pass each other on single track, so set the target headway to 45 minutes so that one train can make the round trip, then confirm.
step11.title: Open the ore freight line

step12.description: Advance time to get mining, loading, rail transport, unloading, and exports going. Procuring vehicles and getting transport up and running takes a few months.
step12.title: Advance time

step13.description: Advance time and check the ore receipts and exports in the coastal Bulk port’s details. Mining, vehicle procurement and transport take several months.
step13.title: Confirm ore exports

tourism.title: Develop tourism
tourism.description: The island needs a harbor, accommodation, and a bus route to welcome visitors to its ruins. Learn to build a hotel and passenger terminal, create a bus route, and check tourist arrivals, restaurant sales, and bus use.

step1.description: Build a Tourist Hotel on the lot marked in yellow west of the ancient ruins. Since this is a tutorial, construction time is skipped.
step1.title: Build a hotel beside the ruins

step2.description: A harbor is needed to receive tourists. Build a Passenger Terminal on the marked harbor lot.
step2.title: Build a passenger terminal

step3.description: Tourists do not have private cars, so public transport needs to be provided. Open Public Transport → New line and choose Bus Route. Place stops on the roads at the yellow markers in this order: harbor → housing → ruins → housing. Set the fare to 0 and the target headway to 1 minute, then confirm.
step3.title: Create a bus route from the harbor to the ruins

step4.description: Advance time to welcome tourists. Facilities and bus vehicle procurement take a few months to get going.
step4.title: Advance time

step5.description: Check the sales of the restaurant by the ruins and the passengers on the bus route you created. Complete this step when tourists have arrived, restaurant sales exceed their starting level, and the bus has passengers. Advance time further if needed.
step5.title: Check restaurant sales and bus passengers

intro.controls: As the new mayor, help build a city where residents can live well and feel safe. This town has no homes for newcomers yet, and no electricity or water supply. This tutorial teaches your role as mayor, how to advance time, how to read the city’s condition, and the buttons and camera controls, then walks you through preparing roads and parcels, setting a district’s direction, building homes, and supplying electricity and water.
intro.scenario4: We want to connect the residential area and workplaces by railway, but private buildings and a public hospital obstruct the route. In this tutorial you will learn land acquisition, public-facility demolition, elevated track above roads, platforms and stations, a depot, curve and grade adjustment, power connection and opening a service.
intro.trade: A local food factory has asked for help selling its products overseas. The town also wants a way to bring in goods it needs from abroad. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to export food through a port and import goods by freight rail from a neighboring country.
intro.highway: As the town grows, more vehicles will carry people and goods through it. The town wants another route ready so through traffic won't all end up on the local road. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to build an elevated highway over a local road and connect them with ramps to create an interchange.
intro.mining: Valuable resources lie beneath this island, but there is no way to haul them from the mountain to the port. Without transport, the island can't turn that wealth into an industry. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to set up a mine, freight railway, and port to extract ore, transport it, and export it overseas.
intro.tourism: The islanders want to share their ancient inland ruins with more visitors. But they lack a passenger harbor, accommodation, and a bus route from the harbor to town. In this tutorial, you will learn to build a hotel and passenger terminal, create a bus route, and check tourist arrivals, restaurant sales, and bus use.
intro.heading: A Request for the Mayor
intro.reclamation: This tiny reef has no flat ground for a city hall and no land for a power plant. In this tutorial, you will learn to reclaim coastal land, place a city hall, and bring electricity from an offshore wind farm to a substation through a power line.
intro.acquisition: Homes, offices, and a fire station stand between two elevated platforms. In this tutorial, you will learn to plan tracks, acquire private land, demolish a public facility, and complete the connection.

reclamation.title: Reclaim the coast
reclamation.description: This tiny reef has no flat ground for a city hall and no land for a power plant. In this tutorial, you will learn to reclaim coastal land, place a city hall, and bring electricity from an offshore wind farm to a substation through a power line.

step1.title: Plan the reclamation
step1.description: Open the Earthworks tool. Left-click the four yellow markers in order to draw a rectangle from the shore into the sea. Right-click to close it, check that the estimate is for reclamation, and confirm the project.

step2.title: Complete the reclaimed land
step2.description: Use Start to advance at least one month, then press Next. Since this lesson has no construction suppliers, Next skips the remaining reclamation work. The sea inside the project becomes land.
step2.description_week: Use Start to advance at least one week, then press Next. Since this lesson has no construction suppliers, Next skips the remaining reclamation work. The sea inside the project becomes land.

step3.title: Create a parcel on the new land
step3.description: Open the parcel tool and choose Single. Set both Depth and Length to 60 m, click the center of the four markers, and confirm. Keep the parcel inside the reclaimed land, away from the quay, with enough room for a city hall.

step4.title: Place the city hall
step4.description: Open the building tool, select City Hall in the Public Services category, and place it at the center of your new parcel. Placing it founds the city.

step5.title: Lay a road in front of the city hall
step5.description: Now that the city exists, let's prepare electricity. A substation delivers power to buildings connected to it by road, so first lay a road in front of the city hall so that a substation can be built along it. This lesson has no construction suppliers, so the road is completed as soon as you confirm it. Press “Roads, Rail & Infrastructure” on the icon panel to open the construction panel.

step6.title: Create a parcel for the substation
step6.description: Prepare a site for the substation along the road. Open the parcel tool and choose Single. Set both Depth and Length to 25 m, click the center of the four markers, and confirm.

step7.title: Build the substation
step7.description: A substation converts incoming high-voltage electricity into power that buildings can use and distributes it to buildings connected by road. Open the building tool, choose “Electrical Substation” in the “Power Plants” category, and build it on your new parcel. This lesson skips the construction period.

step8.title: Create a parcel at sea
step8.description: There is no land for a power plant on this island, but strong winds blow over the surrounding sea. Wind at sea is stronger and steadier than on land, so an offshore wind farm can generate a lot of power. Open the parcel tool, choose Single, set both Depth and Length to 70 m, click the center of the four markers on the sea, and confirm.

step9.title: Build the offshore wind farm
step9.description: Only facilities meant for the sea can be built on a parcel at sea. Open the building tool, choose “Offshore Wind Farm” in the “Power Plants” category, and build it on the parcel at sea. This lesson skips the construction period.

step10.title: Connect with a power line
step10.description: Finally, carry the wind farm's electricity to the substation on land. Power lines can be strung over the sea on pylons standing in the water. Open “Roads, Rail & Infrastructure” on the icon panel, choose “Power Transmission Line” under “Electricity”, and draw it from the wind farm's connection terminal to the substation's terminal. Once they are connected, this tutorial is complete.

acquisition.title: Land acquisition and metro construction
acquisition.description: Homes, offices, and a fire station stand between two elevated platforms. In this tutorial, you will learn to plan tracks, acquire private land, demolish a public facility, and complete the connection.

step1.title: Connect the platforms with tracks
step1.open: Open the road and railway tool. Connect the two existing platforms with elevated tracks 7 m above the ground.
step1.start: Select Double Track and left-click the inner end of the western platform at the cyan marker. The start snaps to the existing endpoint at a height of 7 m.
step1.end: Left-click the inner end of the eastern platform at the yellow marker. You can plan construction even where the tracks overlap homes and offices.
step1.confirm: Review the estimate and press Confirm. This lesson covers track construction; it does not require setting up a train service.
step1.variant: In the railway category, select the highlighted Double Track card.

step2.title: Observe acquisition and the obstruction
step2.description: Use Start to advance time. Acquisition negotiations begin for private parcels in the track corridor. The fire station at the yellow marker is a public facility, so it cannot be acquired automatically and the tracks remain planned. Inspect parcel and building details to see what is happening.

step3.title: Demolish the fire station explicitly
step3.description: Click the fire station at the yellow marker to open its details, then press Bulldoze to order its removal. Public facilities require your explicit demolition order. Leave the other homes and offices to land acquisition.

step4.title: Wait for acquisition and completion
step4.description: Keep advancing time with Start. Track construction proceeds once private land acquisition and demolition are complete. Connecting the two platforms with completed tracks finishes this tutorial.

tip1.title: Money Makes the City Go Round
tip1.description: City spending on construction and public-sector wages becomes income for businesses and households, supporting shopping and production. Collecting taxes alone won't keep the economy moving. Fund needed services and repairs to put money back into the city.

tip2.title: Playing the Long Game
tip2.description: Citizens who grow up in unsafe surroundings retain a greater tendency to commit crime as adults. Keep policing crime and improving the environment children grow up in. Addressing the roots of poor public safety takes at least a generation.

tip3.title: Make Way!
tip3.description: Firefighters need to reach the scene to help. Even with a fire station available, long distances or congested roads let the damage grow. Review station locations and access routes alongside their budgets.

tip5.title: An Uphill Expense
tip5.description: Building roads on steep slopes takes more work than on flat ground. The shortest route on the map isn't always the cheapest. Compare terrain and construction estimates, and consider a slight detour.

tip6.title: Some Planning Required
tip6.description: More residents and factories mean more demand for power and water. Start building after a shortage appears, and you'll be waiting for completion. Check spare supply capacity before developing a new district.

tip7.title: Haste Makes Waste
tip7.description: Higher speed limits make trips faster but raise the risk of accidents. Sharp curves also need care. Where accidents are frequent, review the road layout and speed limit.

tip8.title: Investing in the Future
tip8.description: A growing population alone won't solve staff shortages at hospitals or advanced factories. Set university specializations and admission capacity to train the needed specialists, and allow time for students to graduate.

tip9.title: Built to Last
tip9.description: Neglected repairs let buildings and roads deteriorate, eventually risking collapse. Fires and collapses also worsen public sentiment, so spending everything on new construction is risky. Keep funds available for repairs and firefighting.

tip10.title: A Little Breathing Room
tip10.description: Closely packed buildings let a fire spread more easily to their neighbors. Alongside fire services, leaving space between buildings helps protect the city.

tip11.title: Dig In
tip11.description: Check resource deposits before choosing sites for mines and oil extraction. Reserves fall as you extract them. A mining town also needs a plan for jobs and tax revenue after its deposits run out.

tip12.title: The City's Cash Cow
tip12.description: The mayor can build housing and commercial buildings to earn rent from tenants. Empty space brings in no rent, so check which uses are in demand, nearby vacancies, and the location before building.

tip13.title: The Taxman Cometh
tip13.description: Tax rates affect business costs and profitability as well as city revenue. Lower taxes on an industry can help you support its growth. When revenue falls short, check each industry's situation before raising taxes across the board.

tip14.title: Always Have a Plan B
tip14.description: When accidents or disasters disable power plants or power lines, the effects spread to factories and residents who depend on electricity. Provide backup facilities and delivery routes for important infrastructure so a single failure doesn't bring the whole city to a halt.

tip15.title: Sprawl Has Entered the Chat
tip15.description: When housing or other demand exceeds available buildable parcels, private development adds roads and parcels, causing unplanned sprawl. Prepare roads and parcels where you want growth, with building regulations suited to their intended uses.

tip16.title: Industrial Clusters
tip16.description: Clustering similar industries and their raw-material producers makes a location more favorable for production. Consider grouping related industries instead of scattering factories across the city. Near housing, remember the noise and air pollution they can create.

tip17.title: Rise and Grind
tip17.description: Longer working hours in the Regulations panel let the same workforce support more production. But health and leisure suffer, reducing spending on entertainment. Too much time earning money leaves no time to spend it.

tip18.title: Eat, Commute, Sleep, Repeat
tip18.description: Long commutes cut leisure time and spending on entertainment. Review the distance between homes and jobs, and congestion along the way. To residents who only get home in time to sleep, your lively shopping district is just scenery through a window.

tip19.title: Leave Room to Grow
tip19.description: Longer trains can only run if they fit the platforms at the line's stations. Plan platform lengths when building stations to allow for future demand. Lengthening one station won't help if the others are still too short.

tip20.title: Sweep It Under the City
tip20.description: Underground roads produce no noise or air pollution, making them an option for protecting residential areas. Some problems really can be swept under the city.

tip21.title: In the Shadow of Progress
tip21.description: Tall buildings cast shadows to their north, worsening nearby living conditions. Mind their height and spacing. Terrain such as mountains also casts shadows. Your city's future may be bright, but the ground beneath it might be pitch-black.

tip22.title: Trade the Keys for a Transit Pass
tip22.description: When public transport makes workplaces, schools, and shops easy to reach, households are more likely to choose life without a car. Savings on car ownership can go toward other spending.

tip23.title: Next Stop: Nobody
tip23.description: Buses add road traffic even with no passengers. Running too many can make congestion worse. Check ridership and headways to decide how much service is needed.

tip24.title: Moles Pay No Rent
tip24.description: Deep enough tunnels can pass without buying the land above. Shallow sections still require land acquisition, so check depths and estimates. If negotiations get difficult, try digging a little deeper.

tip25.title: A Suspended Commute
tip25.description: Ropeways can provide public transport where mountains and steep slopes make roads difficult. Provide access to stations and connections to other transport too. If travel on the ground is too much trouble, leave your citizens hanging.

tip26.title: Current Traffic Conditions
tip26.description: Spare generating capacity won't help if power lines cannot carry enough electricity. Before adding power plants, check connections and transmission capacity to the district with the shortage. One undersized line may be limiting the whole city's supply.

tip27.title: Nothing to See Here
tip27.description: You can blow up a building in the way of development and pass it off as an accident. Public sentiment will suffer badly, though. Before clearing a site, weigh the cost of buying and demolishing it against the impact of a forceful approach.

tip28.title: Take to the Sea
tip28.description: Short on land? Reclaim new sites from the sea. Oil platforms can also be built where there are resources beneath the seabed.

tip29.title: Red Light, Red Light
tip29.description: More signal-controlled junctions mean more time waiting at lights. Avoid too many on major roads. With a meticulously intersecting grid, the sun might set before your residents ever see green.

tip30.title: Can You Hear Me Now?
tip30.description: Taller radio towers on higher ground can cover wider areas. Check for mountains between the tower and places without reception. You can't get a signal through a mountain by sheer enthusiasm for more power.

tip31.title: Just Add Power
tip31.description: A coastal desalination plant can supply a city with no nearby fresh water source. It needs electricity to operate, though. First you hunt for water, then you hunt for power.

tip32.title: Jobs on the Beat
tip32.description: Unemployment is one factor that worsens public safety. Residents need jobs as well as police protection. If unemployment is high, check vacancies, the skills employers need, and whether residents can reach those jobs.

tip33.title: That's Future Me's Problem
tip33.description: Buildings and roads keep needing repairs after construction. Expand just because you can afford to build, and future budgets may disappear into upkeep. Remember, the future mayor is also you.

tip34.title: More Pumps, Same Water
tip34.description: Water sources replenish over time, but extracting more than they recover reduces reserves. Secure other sources before demand grows. More pumps don't come with more water.

tip35.title: It's a Feature
tip35.description: Roads and buildings aren't easy to move once construction starts. Before confirming, check orientation, connections, and the land left around them. Still, that accidentally crooked road might grow on you as local character.

tip36.title: Big Mayor Is Watching
tip36.description: Click a pedestrian or car to add a citizen to your tracking list. Use it to follow a resident whose life interests you. Alongside citywide statistics, you can see your city through one person's daily life.

tip37.title: A Backup for the Forecast
tip37.description: Solar and wind output changes with the weather. Planning around good-weather supply alone can leave you short when conditions change. Combine them with sources less dependent on weather, such as thermal or nuclear power.

tip38.title: Size Matters
tip38.description: Some buildings won't fit on small parcels. Check the space needed for a planned facility before dividing the land. Plenty of spare land is no help to a large building if it's all in tiny parcels.

tip39.title: That'll Cost You
tip39.description: Sewage treatment, waste disposal, communications, and healthcare may be free by default. Setting fees lets users cover part of the operating costs. Friendly prices or ambitious price tags? That's the mayor's call.

tip40.title: Copy, Paste, Profit
tip40.description: As mayor, you can construct copies of existing buildings. Keep the type and floor count unchanged and use a parcel that fits the original to reduce construction costs. The streetscape may look repetitive, but your wallet will enjoy the view.

tip41.title: More Than the Rent
tip41.description: Residents compare rent, work and school commutes, shopping trips, housing quality, and the living environment when choosing a new home. Noise, air pollution, public safety, and sunlight all matter. Cheap but inconvenient homes are less appealing; convenient ones still need affordable rent and enough room to move in.

tip42.title: Better Deep Than Sorry
tip42.description: Large ports, such as container, bulk, and tanker ports, need sufficiently deep water. Coasts where the seabed slopes steeply are well suited to ports because deep water is close to shore. Even on a flat coast with shallow water stretching offshore, you can build a port by reclaiming land out to deeper water.

tip43.title: Just a Minute…
tip43.description: Too much on-street parking slows traffic and increases the risk of accidents. Build parking lots to give those cars somewhere else to stay. One driver's “just a minute” can become everyone else's afternoon.

hint.buildingConstruction: Select a parcel to plan a building. It takes some time from planning to completion.
hint.parcelCreation: Hold Ctrl to pick a creation method from the radial menu, then click a target in the 3D view. Adjust the size in the panel and confirm.
hint.transitCreation: Left-click to place stops in order; click the first stop to close the loop. Drag a segment to add a waypoint, drag a point to move it, right-click to delete. For a round trip, also place the return stops.
hint.transitManagement: List of public transit lines. Adjust fares and headways, or create and delete lines. Fares affect residents' route choice. Fares that are too high reduce ridership and increase car ownership.
hint.pathConstruction: Construct roads and railways. Click on the terrain in the 3D view: left-click to add vertices, right-click to confirm the shape, and drag vertices to reposition them. Hold Ctrl to open the settings menu (curve/straight and snapping). Use 3/4 keys to change embankment/cut height.
hint.pathConstructionElevated: Construct roads and railways. Click on the terrain in the 3D view: left-click to add vertices, right-click to confirm the shape, and drag vertices to reposition them. Hold Ctrl to open the settings menu (curve/straight and snapping). Use PageUp/PageDown or 1/2 to change height, and 3/4 keys to change embankment/cut height.
hint.districtEdit: Create, expand and merge "districts", the units for regulations and statistics. Hold Ctrl in the 3D view to switch tools. Create tool: left-click a road to create a new district in the shown color (a new color is drawn each time you pick the tool). Expand tool: right-click to pick the district to grow, then left-click roads to pull them into it. Merge tool: right-click to pick the district to merge into, then left-click another district to open the confirmation panel. The selected district's color and name are shown next to the mouse cursor. Press the button again to exit.
hint.bulldozer: Bulldozer mode. Left-click to remove empty parcels, planned buildings, planned roads, and terrain props (scattered props are removed as a whole area after confirmation). Press the button again to exit.
hint.bulldozerInstant: Bulldozer mode. Left-click to instantly delete buildings, roads, empty parcels, and terrain props with no confirmation. Buildings are removed together with their tenants and residents, and terrain is not restored (the city hall, the border checkpoint, and public transit segments cannot be deleted; scattered props are still removed as a whole area after confirmation). Press the button again to exit.
hint.cityBudget: Decide how to allocate the funds earned from taxes and business operations for the next period. When the government purchases materials for road construction or public facility operations, it can only do so within the budget decided here. If the budget is insufficient, employees of public facilities may be dismissed.
hint.resourceEdit: Create a natural resource area. Select a resource type, then click on the terrain. Left-click to add a vertex, click an edge to insert a vertex, and right-click to remove a vertex. Drag a vertex to reposition it.
hint.grading: Left-click to place vertices, then right-click to confirm the area.
